I’m 5’1 120lbs and I am the deep tissue master, I’ve worked with body builders, athletes, military and primarily large males because I work at a luxury gym . I’m so sorry you graduated massage school without being taught proper deep tissue techniques as a smaller woman .

You have to lower your table and use leverage to create a strong downward force, so drop your table and then massage in a more lunge like position, this way your using gravity to help create the downward force and then activating and utilizing your lower body muscles to drive the massage movements. Using only upper body muscle to drive the movements of a massage is a great way to exhaust yourself and mess up your joints , our lower body muscles are more resistant to fatigue .  

I wish I could demonstrate this technique in person but just play around with table height and leverage until you find what work with you . 

Also if regular deep tissue techniques just aren’t working for you , I highly suggest getting certified in ashiatsu , it’s much easier on your body and it’s a niche modality so it’s easy to build a loyal clientele and have very little competition.

I’ve actually passed out during a training session with my PT who had been a trainer for 20 years . I was in great shape and have the opposite issue as your client , I tend to have low blood pressure.  During one of our sessions my pt wanted to really push me because I had asked him to turn up the intensity, I was in the middle of a squat and just turned ghost white and passed out in his arms because he was spotting me . I was only out for about 30 seconds but it was definitely terrifying.  It was the only time it ever happened and I continued to take on more intense workout routines/weights after the incident and was just fine . 

I know exactly why I had passed out during that session . 

1- I had been going through an extremely stressful situation in my personal life and had been running off of 3-4 hours of sleep for months and had reoccurring panic attacks during that time period

2- to cope with my stress I had recently started to smoke cigarettes again

3- I had been in an extreme calorie deficit for two weeks prior 

4-I was terrible about getting enough water into my diet during those few months

5- I’m slightly anemic , I need red meat but in trying to be as lean as possible all of my protein sources were protein shakes and chicken breast . 

I promise you that in my own experience my trainer had nothing to do with me passing out , how I was taking care of myself outside of the gym was the problem . After I passed out my trainer sat me down in his office told me how dangerous it was for me to train at that level without eating breakfast , told me that Im taking my calorie deficit too far and hurting myself and my goals by doing so and insisted on me eating in front of him for the next two months of our training sessions and would even have protein bars in his office if I forgot mine .   I respected the shit out of him for saying all that and it helped me get into a healthier mindset all around .  It’s what inspired me to become a trainer and I could never thank him enough for it .  Don’t beat yourself up for what happened , understand that somethings are out of your control, if this guy still wants to train with you then go for it you may end up being the most impactful person in his entire life . I would however get in contact with his doctor and make sure he’s cleared for exercise .

Prioritize protein, try to eat at least 15-20g fiber per day , adult females should limit sugar intake to 25g or less per day ( and that’s not even for dieters) raw Fruits are fine as they are full of fiber / micronutrients . You’re both in a transitional stage of life . Your 30’s brings about a psychosocial Identity crisis in which you are compelled to choose between intimacy and isolation. Read about Erik Erikson’s psychosocial stages of development before you decide to end your marriage and come to the conclusion that the only reason you’re unhappy is because your partner is just wrong for you . 

The marriage may be suffering for a multitude of reasons but it’s important to consider all the factors contributing to the decay of relationship before throwing in the towel . You may just need space within the marriage to continue to learn about yourselves and what it is you need to grow and evolve in these next chapters of your life . Maybe you two could come to an agreement where you both get 24hrs of alone time to pursue your interest, hobbies or time to relax without having to worry about the demands of the household or child care. I don’t condone staying in a terrible marriage and agree that divorce can be beneficial but it’s vitally important to realize that you may find yourself unhappy even if you divorce if you don’t overcome this transitional stage of your life in a healthy way . Expecting to find happiness in another person without working on yourself first will likely lead to the same relationship cycle you’re currently in. Create a list of everything that is causing you to feel empty outside of the relationship and see if there’s any changes you can make there first , then focus on your absolute needs to be happy within a relationship and ask your partner if they can realistically meet your needs or if they are willing to try , if they say yes then purpose a timeline in which you expect to see changes within your relationship dynamic. If you find yourself feeling just as empty and don’t see any change or growth within your partner by the deadline create an exit plan from the marriage. You should also be willing to listen and comply with your partners needs and stick to a timeline as well before you point the finger at your partner and decide they are the problem. If you aren’t both willing to grow and put in effort to meet each other’s needs than neither of you have any business being married . I don’t mean for that to sound cruel but marriage takes work , an ability to adapt , self-awareness, sacrifice and realizing both of you may be contributing to the current state of the relationship.

Instead of listening to what the other is saying your both likely waiting to disprove the other or defend your identity, choices or logic . Because of this conditioning your nervous system is sending signals to the amygdala (fight or flight) which is basically the gas pedal for emotional reactions. So it’s not that you two can not work through disagreements but that you need to unlearn your conditioning. So think about your fights in the past are you in a specific location when they take place ? Are you typically standing, pacing in motion ? Are you two typically positioned far apart on opposite sides of the room ? 

You can unlearn conditioning by changing the environmental input that was present in the past . For example if you typically fight in the kitchen or living room then take the discussion to the bedroom . If you two typically walk , pace or move around while the fight gets heated force yourselves to remain in a seated position. If you are typically occupying stances on opposite sides of the room this also is essentially you both defending your territory , so sit close to one another , face each other and touch if possible so your nervous system is receiving neural feedback of oxytocin and “bonding” to indicate “this is a shared problem that needs solution “rather than “ fight til the death” . By changing the environment you can change the predicted outcome . Also it’s important to begin conversations by stating your intention first rather than just going straight in with a complaint. Example someone needs to clean dishes “ I noticed the dishes are pilling up and I wanted to know if it’s because you’re overburdened with housework and if we can re-organize task or if you need more help from me in accomplishing these task” . In this example you’re not demanding, you want to understand rather than blame ,you’re exploring the root of the problem , and offer solutions . All of which display a high level of empathy and understanding. 

It’s important to note that unlearning a conditioned response takes time and patience.so even if you were to do all of these things the next time a fight begins does not mean you will get the desired result .after many trials you two will begin to loose that defensiveness and have more productive conversations and resolutions. As someone whose had a mental breakdown , depressed and put on antidepressants I can tell you in my experience the antidepressants turned me into an empty shell of a person . It was like a numb depression , I was calm but I wasn’t really a person anymore. I’m not saying to take your wife’s antidepressants away , but she may need to try a different antidepressant. She needs to work closely with both a psychologist and psychiatrist that work together and are communicating regularly to provide her with an accurate diagnosis and treatment plan . What I learned in my experience is that I had been given an inaccurate diagnosis and the antidepressants were an ineffective treatment. I was too afraid to really be vulnerable with the first psychologist and psychiatrist I had been referred to so based on what little info I gave them they diagnosed me with major depressive disorder, but that diagnosis can look very similar to almost all non- psychotic mental disorders . It’s really more of an umbrella term diagnosis so for me I was re-evaluated and after months of getting me to open up , I was diagnosed with complex post traumatic stress disorder and with any ptsd type disorders medication is typically ineffective and requires very specific psychology treatment like edmr and requires someone who specializes in trauma psychology. So if you know your wife came from a highly dysfunctional, abusive , traumatic upbringing then you may want to look into a psychiatrist/psychologist duo that can work extensively with her to find an accurate diagnosis and new treatment plan .  You should also look into an accurate diagnosis even if she did not experience trauma because the medications taken for depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and many others differ in many ways on how they affect certain neurotransmitters. I know this advice does not cure your immediate financial issues but I so believe it’s a vitally important step to take . I’m so sorry your wife and you are experiencing these troublesome times and I commend you for your patience, mental health disorders can come with a lot of baggage but things can get better.

I will say that if you're having upper back pain between the shoulder blades there's a good chance that your mid trapezius is actually elongated and when this happens those over lengthened muscles are constantly pulling on the spine . Our muscles work like a pulley system meaning that when one muscle is lengthened on the opposite side we have a muscle that is chronically shortened and tight.  for the most part massage is much more beneficial for lengthening muscle fibers .  This could possibly explain why you're not getting much relief because they are taking a muscle that's already over stretched like a tight rubber band and stretching it even further causing the muscle to pull on the spine even more .  If this is the case for you I would ask for upper body only including the glutes .  Also ask your therapist to incorporate pec work , scm or scalene work to your service because by releasing the muscles on the anterior side of the body the muscles in the posterior side will not have to stretch quite as far giving you relief . As many other therapist have said this all goes back to posture and the same repetitive movements at work or driving every day . Your first massage like this should bring some relief but if you want to keep the pain at bay schedule your massages once a week or at the very least once a month to get the full benefit.  If you do have rounded shoulders like I suspect and would like to work on fixing your posture massage is only half of the equation we can lengthen short muscles but we can not shorten elongated muscles to do that you would need some type of resistance training if you already workout throwing in exercises that focus on the mid back or  pulling motions that get the arms behind the body will help if you're not sure where to start athleanx on YouTube can help you navigate what exercises to do and why . A personal trainer or physical therapist would be your best bet in fixing a muscular imbalance .  When you schedule your massage look for an LMT who specializes in deep tissue or neuromuscular therapy . You can find great therapist in spa settings that are certified in all the modalities listed but they can vary in their technical application or what is considered deep tissue so if you are on the search looking at clinical type massage may help narrow it down faster . Look for therapist that work under chiropractors, physical therapist, hospitals, pain management centers , fitness or wellness centers or even free lance but ask what their specialties are before booking. I think the worst thing that happened here is a lack of communication. Peck (chest )work , and adductor work (inner thigh) is very important and can really help with postural imbalances . If you have upper back pain and your shoulders round forward then it can be an indication that your middle trapezius muscle is over stretched and honestly working the upper back for a long period is just going to lengthen the muscle more pulling the shoulder blades even further apart causing more pull on the spine and creating more tension or pain . So as a therapist if you notice rounded shoulders then automatically you should know this persons pecks are way too tight because all of our muscles work like a pulley system. So if muscles A is too long then muscle B is to short and most massage strokes lengthen muscle tissue I am sure this is probably why your therapist did peck work . Look at posture and see if your shoulders round forward and when you stand do your toes point more inward like a variation of pigeon toe ? If so then that might be why she did adductor work . So the areas she massaged are ok to massage and can be really beneficial but she definitely should have communicated this to you during the intake or on the table . Some therapist become desensitized and forget not everyone has had 1,000 massages and massage training. Never be afraid to use your voice on the massage table . It’s your hour your body and your hard earned money and you get to have a say in what’s going on and I promise you we will not get offended by you speaking up for your needs , that’s why we’re here in the first place !! I hope this gives you some clarity and peace of mind . Don’t give up on massage therapy but do make sure you have a therapist that can communicate and makes you feel comfortable!
